design_rationale:
[1 WHY A GOOD TEST] Harold Brennan (Premier Package, independent Two-Bedroom shared with his wife) asks only to move his plan down to "the one that fits what you actually use". The scored value is the target package, which the published fit rule derives from a reconciled 3-month usage figure (delivered hours, late/no-show hours by count, a divisor that depends on suspended months, a home headroom from the independent residency and a last-month trend) compared against the package allotments. The fit's own rule says it is not chosen until every late cancellation or no-show in the review months carries its hours entry; the orders show a 2026-10-09 no-show (SO-2610-1064) with no entry. The agent must post that entry first, computing it through five factors (band, booked-hours basis, cancellation pattern, rebooking relief, Life Plan reduction) to 0.34 hours, and only then fit the package (Comfort, required 8.17). The entry flips the late-use factor from half to full and moves the fit across the 8-hour boundary: skipped, the fit gives Companion.
[2 SCOPE SNAPSHOT] Already occupied by task 0: services_ext_suspension_months + services_ext_short_visit_credit, tools sign_services_suspension_89d6021d / post_services_visit_credit_5ef485c2, subjects services_suspend / services_credit. Claimed here: services_ext_package_fit (root, user tool sign_services_package_change_2a41e92a, subject services_package_change_request) and services_ext_missed_visit_hours (prerequisite, agent tool post_services_order_hours_8d682fe6, subject services_hours_draw). Pairwise disjoint policies, tools and subjects; together the two tasks cover all four extended policies. Factor families are distinct from task 0 (no visit-time rounding, no surcharge; the entrance factor here reduces missed-visit hours, in task 0 it reduces the overage rate - different quantities and wording).
[3 DRAW] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[4, 5]: services_ext_package_fit takes 4, services_ext_missed_visit_hours takes 5. One value_input edge (floor max(0,1)=1).
[4 PROBLEM-TREE CARD] root services_ext_package_fit <- services_ext_missed_visit_hours; kind value_input; gate binding late_hours; form state. Prerequisite sentence (own rule of the root, negated direction - a choice 'is not chosen until' its inputs stand): "The package that fits the resident's use is not chosen until every service order recorded in the review months as a late cancellation or a no-show carries its hours entry for that cancellation on the plan's ledger." Four-point test: connective 'not ... until'; XX a record-visible state (an hours entry on the ledger for the order); no tool, id or code token; scope 'every ... in the review months'. Only the missed-visit policy writes an hours entry for a late-cancelled or missed order ('against that order with its own draw basis'). Derivation: sentence + orders (SO-2610-1064 no-show 2026-10-09) + ledger (no entry with that order number) + the missed-visit rule -> post its hours. False at the opening: initial_state.services_orders.<SO-2610-1064 cancel>.cancellation_type = no_show, no services_ledger row with order_reference SO-2610-1064. Resolving tool owner agent; root tool owner user (Harold signs). Order: step 8 then step 10. Sensitivity: skip -> Companion instead of Comfort. user_scenario names no visit, cancellation or hours; tools validate nothing.
[5 BASE-INVARIANT CARD] Step 8 subject services_hours_draw: services_hours_and_billing one_draw_per_order (dedup on order_reference + draw_basis + event_type: existing late/no-show draws reference SO-2605-1377 and SO-2608-1080 only, so SO-2610-1064 has never been drawn) and services_late_cancellation (cancel_once applies to recording a cancellation, already on record -> policy_scope). The extended policy supersedes the base 24-hour lateness sentence (calendar-day bands) and the no-show sentence (pattern, rebooking and entrance adjustments), declared in overwrite. Step 10 subject services_package_change_request: services_package_change change_while_active (plan status active since the October resume; evidence plan.status). commitment_elapsed applies to the change taking effect, not to the request; the Premier package has run since 2021-01-01, far beyond 3 months. No time gate applies to either write, so temporal_feasibility is empty; the effective date follows the base cutoff rule (signed 2026-10-14 <= day 20 -> 2026-11-01; a request on the 21st would give 2026-12-01).
[6 BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD] Step 8 object: order SO-2610-1064 (errand_shopping, booked 0.75 h for Friday 2026-10-09 10:00 on 2026-10-02, no-show recorded at the start time); the entry carries that order number and billing month 2026-10. Rows read for its factors: the 2026-05-20 no-show draw and 2026-08-21 late-cancellation draw (pattern), the 2026-10-12 errand booking SO-2610-1098 (rebooking), the LifeCare agreement. Excluded: SO-2605-1377 and SO-2608-1080 (already drawn), delivered orders. Step 10 object: the plan; the fit reads draws/charges posted fewer than 3 whole months before 2026-10-14, i.e. from 2026-07-15 (the July draws, posted 2026-07-03, 07-09 and 07-11, fall outside by the rule's stated convention), fees 2026-08-01 and 2026-10-01.
[7 FACTOR CARD - services_ext_missed_visit_hours (5)] missed_visit_band (parameter; no-show -> 1.0; baseline late_cancel_hours_charged 0.5 -> 0.16). missed_visit_basis (method; booked 0.75 < band -> booked hours; baseline band -> 0.52). cancellation_pattern (parameter; 2 entries in 6 months -> x1.2; baseline x1 -> 0.25; near-miss: the 2026-05-20 no-show lies outside the 3-month fit window yet inside the 6-month pattern window, and the August entry is a late cancellation, not a no-show, but both kinds count). rebooking_relief (parameter; most recent same-service booking made 3 days later -> x0.6; baseline x1 -> 0.70; near-miss: 3 days is outside the 2-day quick tier). entrance_hours_reduction (parameter, single EFA record; cross-difficulty entrance -> -0.20; baseline 0 -> 0.54). All-baseline fall-back 0.50. Gold 0.34.
[8 FACTOR CARD - services_ext_package_fit (4)] review_divisor (method; 2 fees in the window, no change -> /2; baseline /3 -> Companion). missed_visit_use (parameter; 2 late/no-show entries -> in full 0.84; baseline none -> Companion; near-miss: before step 8 there is one entry, counted at half). home_headroom (parameter, cross-difficulty independent; Two-Bedroom, double, Margaret Brennan named -> +1.0; baseline 0 -> Companion). use_trend (parameter; last whole month 7.84 >= 5.17 + 2 -> +2.0; baseline 0 -> Companion). All-baseline fall-back Essentials (9.50/3 = 3.17). Gold Comfort (8.17).
[9 WORLD ROWS] customer, active independent residency (Two-Bedroom, double), occupied LifeCare entrance agreement, Premier plan (suspended 2026-09, caches 12.50 h / 829.00 equal the ledger), ledger May-October 2026 (fees, grants, rollovers capped at 10, month-end expiries equal remaining hours, autopays, delivered draws, the May no-show and August late-cancellation draws), orders with book/complete/cancel rows including the open 2026-10-16 errand. Automatic clauses: no fee/grant for suspended September, hours left at its start expired 2026-08-31, no rollover into September or October, October fee not yet due (balance 829.00 = October fee).
[10 PERSONA] Harold, brisk retired engineer; volunteers only the request; identity on request (DOB + phone, email, SSN4 only if pressed); passive: Margaret also uses the plan; September at his son's; 'go ahead' to any posting; accepts the fitted package; signs with the agent's values; ends. Never states hours, visits or a package.
[11 STANDARD SOLUTION] find_customers(name) -> verify (DOB + phone) -> find_services_plans -> find_services_ledger -> find_services_orders -> find_independent_residencies -> find_entrance_agreements -> unlock + call post_services_order_hours_8d682fe6(plan, SO-2610-1064, no_show, services_hours_draw, 2026-10, 0.34, 0.0) -> unlock_user + call_user sign_services_package_change_2a41e92a(plan, Personal Services Comfort Package, 2026-11-01).
[12 VERIFICATION RUN] /tmp/psp2/sens.py 1 (temporary, removed; round 2): hours 0.34; factor baselines 0.16/0.52/0.25/0.70/0.54; all-baseline 0.50; fit Comfort; factor baselines Companion x4; all-baseline Essentials; skipping the draw -> Companion. Gates --task 1: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK (79/79), SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.
[13 DRAFT RECOMPUTE FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT] From the fit document (lowest package covering average use) and the factor documents reached from the records (suspended month, late entries, shared Two-Bedroom, rising October) a reader gets 8.17 once the no-show is drawn; the prerequisite sentence sends him to SO-2610-1064, whose documents give 0.34 hours as a draw. Same writes as gold; no second reading (the open 2026-10-16 errand is not cancelled, so it is not a missed order).
[14 REVISIONS] r1: the event_type enum had to describe every schema literal (gate) -> each ledger kind described, the two that apply explained; target_variant_name enum gained the 'none' literal. r2: the entrance ladder wording was made specific to missed-visit hours to keep it distinct from task 0's overage-rate ladder.

[15 ROUND-2 REWORK (audit policy_task/personal_services_packages)] F-2 / SOURCE-TASK RED: the fit rule now states the window convention (a posting is within the review months when fewer than review_months whole months have elapsed from its posting date to the request date, a whole month elapsing on the same day of each later month; same-day-of-month 3 months earlier is outside, the next day inside; the last whole month counted the same way), and the boundary row was moved: order SO-2607-1121 is now a 2026-07-10 visit drawn 2026-07-11, 3 whole months and 3 days before the request, outside under every reading. O-4: the divisor sentence no longer carries the causal 'because the plan was suspended' (now 'as when the plan was suspended for a month'). O-3: the rebooking factor is read from the most recent booking of the same service, matching compute. O-7: the band ladder's fall-through is now a case the write handles (a cancellation received on the visit's own day -> late_cancel_hours_charged, the published standard); a cancellation received on the day before draws late_cancel_hours_charged x day_before_share 0.5; cancellations two or more days ahead are stated out of scope. Rounding observation: the multipliers were re-set (repeat 1.2, rebooking week 0.6) so that no scored or proof figure lands on a half-hundredth: hours 0.34 (was 0.27), required 8.17, sensitivity 0.16 / 0.52 / 0.25 / 0.70 / 0.54, all-baseline 0.50; skip-edge required 7.875 gives 7.88 under both binary and half-up rounding. Label: entrance_hours_reduction is a single-record factor (multi-source factors here: rebooking_relief, review_divisor, use_trend). Re-run: fit Comfort; factor baselines Companion x4; all-baseline Essentials; skip draw Companion.
[16 ROUND-4 REWORK (render-layer audits policy_kb / runtime_context)] B3/N6: the 'last whole month' window left the fit's baseline review-months sentence and now lives only in the trend factor's own sentence, stated in full (less than one whole month from posting date to request date, a whole month elapsing on the same day of the next month). N7: the fit rule states that an independent living resident whose required hours exceed every allotment is fitted to the Concierge Package (what the compute already did). N8: the missed-visit scope sentence states that lateness is read in calendar days and late_cancel_notice_hours plays no part. N5: lifecare / fee-for-service contracts named by plan. Values unchanged: 0.34 hours, Personal Services Comfort Package; sensitivity unchanged.
user_scenario: You are Harold Brennan, 85, an independent living resident at Larkspur at Willow Creek in Plano, where you share a two-bedroom apartment with your wife Margaret. You are calling the Resident and Family Services desk yourself; you are brisk, a retired engineer who likes short answers, and you manage your own account. You are on the Premier personal services package and you feel you and Margaret do not come close to using the hours you pay for. You want the plan moved to a smaller package - whichever package actually fits what the two of you use. You do not know the package names or how many hours each gives, and you are not going to pick one yourself; you want the desk to work out the right one and you will sign for it. You want the change to start as soon as the rules allow. Open by giving your name and saying you would like to move your personal services package down to the one that fits what you actually use. You give identifying details only when asked: your full name is Harold Brennan, your date of birth is 1941-06-22, and your phone number is 4695550123; if an email is asked for it is harold.brennan41@outlook.com. You do not give your Social Security number over the phone unless the agent says nothing else will do, in which case the last four digits are 9137. If the agent asks whether Margaret also uses the services, you say yes, the plan covers the two of you. If the agent asks about your time away, you say you were at your son's in Colorado for September and the package was paused for that month. If the agent says something on the account has to be posted or brought up to date before the package can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead and do whatever the records need; you have no idea what it would be and you do not ask for details beyond what the agent offers. When the agent tells you which package fits and when it starts, you accept it without arguing, even if it is not as small as you expected. When the agent hands you the change to sign, you sign it with exactly the plan, the package and the start date the agent gives you, and you read back what the confirmation shows. Once the agent confirms the change is scheduled, you thank them and hang up. You never say how many hours you think you use, never mention any particular visit, missed appointment or cancellation, and never suggest which package it should be.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.services_plan_id: af03ebad-416b-44a1-a280-d3bb9e71666f — basis: the Id-class contract 'the reference number of the personal services plan the order belongs to, as returned by the personal services plan lookup'; uniqueness: the resident holds one plan.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.order_reference: SO-2610-1064 — basis: the missed-visit hours rule 'one order at a time beginning with the most recently recorded cancellation or no-show' and the orders read: the cancellation records are SO-2605-1377 (no-show, drawn 2026-05-20), SO-2608-1080 (late cancellation, drawn 2026-08-21) and SO-2610-1064 (no-show 2026-10-09, no hours entry); uniqueness: SO-2610-1064 is the most recent and the only one without an entry; copied verbatim from the order record.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.draw_basis: no_show — basis: the rule 'against that order with its own draw basis' and the docstring 'no_show when staff arrived and the resident declined the service or was absent'; the order's cancellation record has cancellation_type no_show; uniqueness: service_delivered needs a completion record (none) and late_cancellation needs a resident cancellation (the record is a no-show).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.event_type: services_hours_draw — basis: the rule 'they are taken from the plan's available hours, or charged at hourly_rate_beyond_allotment where no hours remain' and the docstring 'services_hours_draw when the hours are taken from the plan's available hours'; the plan shows 12.50 hours available; uniqueness: services_hourly_charge applies only when no hours remain, and the other listed kinds are not an order's hours.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.billing_period: 2026-10 — basis: the rule 'the billing month of its service date' and the docstring 'the month of the service date'; the missed visit was scheduled 2026-10-09; uniqueness: copied from the service date.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.hours: 0.34 — calculated by services_ext_missed_visit_hours: band no_show_hours_charged 1.0 (Premier); basis = booked 0.75 because it is below the band; pattern multiplier 1.2 for two late/no-show entries in six months (2026-05-20, 2026-08-21); rebooking multiplier 0.6 because the most recent errand_shopping booking was made 2026-10-12, 3 days after the visit; entrance reduction 0.20 for an occupied LifeCare agreement; 0.75 x 1.2 x 0.6 - 0.20 = 0.34.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 0.0 — basis: the docstring 'for an hours charge the money billed in USD ...; 0.00 when the entry takes hours from the plan's available hours'; uniqueness: the entry is a draw (event_type services_hours_draw), so no money is billed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The resident signs the change to the Personal Services Comfort Package from 2026-11-01, recorded on the plan as a scheduled change.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: services_ext_package_fit computes target_variant_name on the world after the missed-visit hours have landed.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.services_plan_id: af03ebad-416b-44a1-a280-d3bb9e71666f — basis: the Id-class contract of the change tool and the plan lookup; uniqueness: one plan.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.target_variant_name: Personal Services Comfort Package — calculated by services_ext_package_fit on the world after the step-8 entry: hours used in the review months (postings fewer than 3 whole months before 2026-10-14, i.e. from 2026-07-15) = 9.50 delivered + 0.84 late/no-show (two entries, counted in full) = 10.34; divisor 2 (only the 2026-08-01 and 2026-10-01 fees, September suspended); average 5.17; +1.0 headroom for a Two-Bedroom in double occupancy with Margaret Brennan named; +2.0 trend because the last whole month shows 7.84 hours, at least 2.0 above the average; required 8.17 -> the lowest package with at least 8.17 monthly hours is the Comfort Package (12).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.pending_change_date: 2026-11-01 — basis: the fit rule 'the signed change takes effect on the first day of the next month when signed on or before change_notice_cutoff_day of the month' with change_notice_cutoff_day 20 and the request signed 2026-10-14; uniqueness: 14 <= 20 so the next month applies; a later month would contradict the rule.

edges.condition: Every services_orders cancellation row with cancellation_type no_show, or a resident cancellation received on the visit's day or the day before, within the review window has a services_hours_draw or services_hourly_charge row on the plan with the same order_reference and draw_basis no_show or late_cancellation.
edges.policy_source: The package that fits the resident's use is not chosen until every service order recorded in the review months as a late cancellation or a no-show carries its hours entry for that cancellation on the plan's ledger.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Order SO-2610-1064 carries a no-show record dated 2026-10-09, inside the review window, and no ledger entry with order_reference SO-2610-1064 exists.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The step-8 draw of 0.34 hours with draw_basis no_show and order_reference SO-2610-1064 lands; late-cancellation/no-show hours in the window rise from 0.50 (one entry, counted at half = 0.25) to 0.84 (two entries, counted in full), the average from 4.875 to 5.17 and the required hours from 7.88 to 8.17.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, no parallel prerequisites: the fit reads the late/no-show hours the draw adds, so the draw must land first; in the reverse order the fit gives the Companion Package instead of the Comfort Package (sensitivity run).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the draw leaves one late entry (counted at half), average 4.875, required 7.88 (7.875 half up) -> target_variant_name Personal Services Companion Package instead of Personal Services Comfort Package; the terminal ledger also lacks the 0.34-hour no-show draw and hours_available stays 12.50 instead of 12.16. With the window convention now stated in the rule, no posting sits on the window boundary (the nearest, 2026-07-11, is 3 whole months and 3 days before the request).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for the package that fits; it says Harold never mentions a visit, missed appointment or cancellation and never names hours or a package; on the agent's statement that something must be posted first he only consents.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: sign_services_package_change_2a41e92a only updates pending_variant_name / pending_change_date with what it is given and reads no ledger; post_services_order_hours_8d682fe6 books whatever hours it is passed; neither checks a prerequisite, refuses or hints.

factor_trace: missed_visit_band (parameter): order SO-2610-1064 has a cancellation record of type no_show dated 2026-10-09 -> no_show_hours_charged of the Premier Package = 1.0; the baseline (band = late_cancel_hours_charged 0.5, the same-day-cancellation tier) gives basis 0.5 (booked 0.75 is not below it) x 1.2 x 0.6 - 0.20 = 0.16.
missed_visit_basis (method): the order booked 0.75 hours, fewer than the 1.0 band hours -> basis = booked hours 0.75; the baseline (band hours as they stand) gives 1.0 x 1.2 x 0.6 - 0.20 = 0.52.

cancellation_pattern (parameter): late-cancellation/no-show hours entries posted fewer than 6 whole months before 2026-10-14: 2026-05-20 no-show draw and 2026-08-21 late-cancellation draw = 2 -> repeat_multiplier 1.2; the baseline 1 gives 0.75 x 0.6 - 0.20 = 0.25.

rebooking_relief (parameter): the most recent errand_shopping booking was made 2026-10-12 09:20 (order SO-2610-1098), 3 days after the missed 2026-10-09 visit -> more than 2 and at most 7 days -> rebook_week_multiplier 0.6; the baseline 1 gives 0.90 - 0.20 = 0.70.
entrance_hours_reduction (parameter, cross-difficulty entrance): occupied LifeCare Declining Balance Plan, contract_type lifecare -> 0.20 hours; the baseline 0 gives 0.54.
plumbing: miss_ref = SO-2610-1064 (most recent cancellation/no-show record, cancelled_at 2026-10-09 10:00); result = RND(MX(0, 0.75 x 1.2 x 0.6 - 0.20), 2) = 0.34 (no rounding tie).

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: the order was recorded as a no-show
the order booked fewer hours than the band hours
at least two late-cancellation or no-show hours entries in the last repeat_lookback_months months
the most recent booking of the same service was made more than rebook_quick_days and at most rebook_week_days days after the missed visit date
the resident whose visit was missed holds an occupied Entrance Fee Agreement on a lifecare contract

factor_trace: review_divisor (method): package fees posted fewer than 3 whole months before 2026-10-14 are 2026-08-01 and 2026-10-01 (2026-07-01 is 3 whole months and 13 days before, outside; September suspended), no package_change fee -> divide by 2; the baseline (divide by 3) gives average 3.45, trend +2, headroom +1 -> 6.45 -> Personal Services Companion Package.

missed_visit_use (parameter): late-cancellation/no-show entries in the window: 2026-08-21 (0.50) and the step-8 entry for SO-2610-1064 (0.34) = 2 -> counted in full 0.84; the baseline (none counted) gives 9.50/2 = 4.75 + 1 + 2 = 7.75 -> Companion.

home_headroom (parameter, cross-difficulty independent): active Independent Living Two-Bedroom, double occupancy, second occupant Margaret Brennan -> home_headroom_shared 1.0; the baseline 0 gives 7.17 -> Companion.

use_trend (parameter): hours drawn and charged posted fewer than 1 whole month before 2026-10-14 (2026-09-15 onward) = 7.50 delivered + 0.34 = 7.84, which is at least 2.0 above the 5.17 average -> +2.0; the baseline 0 gives 6.17 -> Companion.

plumbing: delivered hours in the window 9.50 (2026-08-06 2.00; October 2.00+2.00+2.00+1.50; the July draws posted 2026-07-03, 07-09 and 07-11 are 3 or more whole months before and outside); used 10.34; average 5.17; required RND(5.17 + 1.0 + 2.0, 2) = 8.17; independent residence; lowest package whose allotment is at least 8.17 = Personal Services Comfort Package (12 hours).

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: no package change took effect and fewer than review_months package fees were posted in the review months
at least two late-cancellation or no-show hours entries posted in the review months
it is any other apartment type held in double occupancy and a second occupant is named
hours drawn and charged in the last whole month are at least trend_gap_hours above the average monthly use
